A1.justification: Both readable, 14-page PDFs describe the same PAGE-4D study and support comparison of its text, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains appendix pages or embedded appendices, despite appendix references; those references do not establish additional available evidence.

before.justification: Tables 1–5 report original PAGE-4D results for depth estimation, camera poses, point reconstruction, view synthesis and fine-tuning/masking ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains the original PAGE-4D experimental results and ablations, alongside an expanded point-reconstruction comparison.

M1.justification: Equation 5 changes from -alpha*sigmoid(-m/tau) to alpha*sigmoid(m/tau). These differ by a constant alpha on patch entries, but unspecified padding for camera/register tokens prevents establishing equivalence of the full attention operation. The new augmented-Q/K/V implementation is described as equivalent, so its disclosure alone does not establish an underlying method change.

E1.justification: Both retain the same depth, pose, point-reconstruction and rendering tasks on Sintel, Bonn, DyCheck, TUM and Nerfie, plus the Odyssey diagnostic and KITTI timing evaluation. No additional dataset or task scenario is reported.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Easi3R variants based on DUSt3R and MonST3R, with the latter marked as using optimization. Neither appeared in v1's corresponding comparison, although Easi3R was already cited and discussed. Other comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Benchmark metrics, depth alignment, Sim(3) trajectory alignment, 10-frame sampling and timing settings remain unchanged. However, Figure 2 changes the stated visualization layers from 4/11/17/23 to 5/12/18/24 without explaining whether this corrects indexing or changes the inspected layers.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 and Table 5 retain the same whole-model versus middle-layer fine-tuning comparison and mask ablation, with identical outcomes. The motivation analysis and displayed attention patterns are retained; Figure 2's relabeling does not supply a new analysis. Neither PDF includes the additionally referenced appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table 3's mean/median error summaries and the reporting practices elsewhere remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds two six-metric Easi3R result rows. Their overall mean errors are 1.088 for the DUSt3R variant and 1.247 for the MonST3R variant. The former introduces a lower median completion error than PAGE-4D, 0.586 versus 0.728. All previously reported numerical entries, including PAGE-4D's results and ablations, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.2 adds a derivation showing how augmented Q/K/V vectors produce an additive logit bias r_i*c_j, together with an argument for linear rather than quadratic mask storage. The existing static/dynamic geometry equations and reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The new introduction contribution list restates the existing VGGT adaptation, dynamics-aware aggregator and targeted fine-tuning contributions. The abstract and conclusion retain the same scientific scope and performance, efficiency and generalization claims.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains that explicitly materializing the attention mask incurs quadratic storage and obstructs fused attention, and argues that vector augmentation avoids these constraints. Existing result interpretations, the pose-versus-geometry rationale and the stated exclusion of point tracking remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds the feature scaling and padding recipe for implementing the mask through fused attention. Conversely, Section 3.2 and Figure 3 replace the explicit 8/10/6 stage sizes with N1/N2/N3; the middle 10 layers remain specified elsewhere, but the first and last counts are no longer given. The code/demo link and other disclosed training details are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged. Easi3R was already cited and positioned in v1; adding its numerical comparison does not introduce a new cited work or revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds VGGT to the title, revises affiliations and contribution footnotes, adds contribution bullets and a memory-efficiency paragraph, and removes or replaces unresolved appendix-table references. Most prose and the section hierarchy remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 revises geometric annotations and layer labels, Figure 3 substitutes symbolic stage counts, and Table 3 gains two rows with revised highlighting. Figure 5 and Table 5 relocate as the text reflows. The overall figure/table set and presentation format are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful Easi3R comparison evidence and a concrete memory-saving derivation. However, it removes explicit first/last stage sizes and leaves the changed mask equation's relationship to the full attention operation unresolved. These gains and losses affect reproducibility of the central mechanism, and the unchanged benchmark results do not resolve their net effect on paper quality.
